questions.text: Explain how audiences and profile attributes flow into journeys.
sections: Our approach

Journey Optimizer and Real-Time CDP share Experience Platform profiles, identities and audiences. Journey Optimizer can also run on its own; Real-Time CDP adds its audience and activation tools on the same data.
Email, push, SMS and web experiences are chosen from the same customer profile and audiences; with streaming audiences and events, timing and offers follow recent behavior.
What we would do

We will design and build branching, multi-touch journeys that enter from Real-Time CDP audiences or events, with waits, conditions, exit criteria and configured conditions that route profiles to the agreed channel and content.

We will set up your first event-triggered messages (such as cart, browse or welcome) and scheduled sends that read Real-Time CDP audiences and profile attributes, then test entry, conditions and suppression.
We will design, build, test and publish the starting journeys and campaigns, such as a welcome series, an abandoned cart journey and a scheduled campaign, with entry, wait and exit rules.
We will set the merge method and dataset priority in the default merge policy, review how the identity graph links records, and check sample profiles against source data.

sections: Our approach
We would deliver this with AEM Sites.
What we would do
We will build the site from the AEM Project Archetype or a Site Template, with Core Components, editable templates, client-side libraries and the custom components the design needs.
We will train authors to edit pages and content in the Universal Editor and hand over authoring guides for the site's components and templates.
We will assign AEM product profiles in the Admin Console, create the production program and environments in Cloud Manager, set up Git access and the first deployment pipelines.
After launch
Each month we will ship code through Cloud Manager pipelines, check the automatic AEM version updates, review logs and the Developer Console, and fix issues found after go-live.

questions.label: (ii
questions.text: Explain how you would connect AEM Sites to Target.
sections: Our approach

AEM Sites exports Experience Fragments (HTML or JSON) and Content Fragments (JSON) to Target as offers through an IMS-based Target configuration, and Target runs its activities on AEM pages through the Tags property AEM loads, with Web SDK or at.js.

Authors build offers as Experience Fragments in AEM and marketers use them in Target tests and personalization on AEM pages (not in Multivariate Test or Recommendations activities; JSON and Content Fragment offers only in Form-Based activities), while the content stays managed in AEM.
What we would do

We will set up the Developer Console project and the IMS, Target and legacy Target configurations in AEM, configure the Link Externalizer, set export format, workspace and domain on the fragment folders, and set up the publish, export and update routine for lean Web variations.
We will build the site from the AEM Project Archetype or a Site Template, with Core Components, editable templates, client-side libraries and the custom components the design needs.
We will enable Target in the datastream, add flicker handling, render Visual and Form-based Experience Composer activities, pass profile and entity data, and validate the setup.

AEM Link Externalizer set on author; fragments and their assets published before export
Experience Fragment Web variations; JSON offers only in Form-Based activities
